question: A forecaster says '70% chance of rain' on 100 different days. If they are perfectly calibrated, on how many of those days does it rain?
answer: On about 70. A calibrated forecaster's 70% comes true seven times in ten. Superforecasters are scored this way, with a measure called a Brier score that punishes both overconfidence and timidity. A single rainy or dry day says almost nothing about the forecaster; a hundred say a lot.
move: A forecast is judged over many days, not on one.
simply: If you say 'I'm 7 out of 10 sure' about lots of things, you should be right about 7 of every 10 of them. Not more, not less.
why: It is how this app measures you: saying 80% and being right 80% of the time is what being well calibrated means.
source: Philip Tetlock and Dan Gardner, Superforecasting, 2015
reference: Philip Tetlock and Dan Gardner, Superforecasting (Crown, 2015), ch. 3
